newsitem.title: CHINA: Four banks in Shanghai named to do yuan business.
newsitem.headline: Four banks in Shanghai named to do yuan business.

text.p: Four foreign banks in Shanghai have been named to do local Chinese currency business, a spokesman for the Shanghai branch of the People's Bank of China said on Monday.
The four banks are the Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corp, Citibank, Tokyo-Mitsubishi Bank and the Industrial Bank of Japan, he said.

The spokesman said the foreign banks would be allowed to do Chinese currency loans, deposits, settlements and other business as defined by rules issued recently by the People's Bank, the central bank.
A foreign banker working with one of the banks said the banks had been given formal confirmation today.
"But there were no details at all, no conditions of business given," he said.
On December 12, the official Xinhua news agency reported that the chosen foreign banks would not be allowed to have local currency debts exceeding 35 percent of their foreign currency debts.
Foreign banks are now restricted to business in foreign currency and have been eager to gain a share of the huge local market for deposits and loans in yuan.
Foreign banks would have to adopt the regulations that applied to Chinese financial institutions, Xinhua said.
It did not elaborate but that appeared to mean foreign banks would have to accept the same tax rate used for Chinese banks -- one of the key obstacles to implementing the policy change.
Foreign bank profits are currently taxed at a 15 percent rate while Chinese commercial banks are taxed at 33 percent and the main state banks at 55 percent.
Only banks with branches in the Pudong district east of Shanghai's city centre are eligible to apply for the right to do local currency business.
